disease_label_per_paper: Left-sided community-acquired pneumonia with empyema thoracis managed with ultrasound-guided pigtail catheter
presentation_summary: 66-year-old woman presented with cough for 10 days, fever for 7 days, and pain in the left hypochondrium/chest region for 7 days.
No chronic illnesses such as diabetes, hypertension, or tuberculosis were reported; no previous surgery, regular medications, significant drug allergy, or relevant family history was reported.
Examination showed RR 28/min, pulse 140/min, BP 160/100 mmHg, and SpO2 82% on room air, later maintained at 96% with 5 L oxygen by face mask.
Auscultation showed decreased air entry in the left infrascapular region.
Blood tests showed WBC 18.8 x10^9/L with neutrophils 87% and CRP >150 mg/L.

Chest radiograph showed increased opacity over the left lower lung field with left costophrenic angle obliteration; ultrasound showed left pleural effusion with septations; contrast chest CT showed two communicating loculated left lower-chest collections, largest about 6 x 7 cm, estimated total 380 mL.

actual_treatment.name: 16 Fr ultrasound-guided pigtail catheter via left 9th intercostal space posterolateral approach connected to underwater seal drainage

course_observations.source_text_value: 80 ml pus-like fluid drained immediately with another 400 ml in 24 h
symptoms resolving within 48 h following catheter insertion

outcome_follow_up.description: She tolerated pigtail catheter insertion without complications; 80 mL pus-like fluid drained immediately and 400 mL more in 24 hours. Symptoms resolved within 48 hours, the catheter was removed, repeat imaging showed resolving empyema, she completed medications, was discharged after clinical/radiologic resolution, and continued improving at 7-day follow-up.

quality_warnings: Pleural tap cell count, Gram stain, AFB stain, pus drainage, treatment response, and follow-up are confirmatory/non-ranking.
Ranking evidence preserves initial symptoms, vitals, exam, blood labs, CXR, ultrasound, and CT loculation before drainage.
